records.deidentified_narrative: incident involving an unknown vehicle and a pedestrian in the parking lot of panda express, located at 728 west sh 71, bastrop, texas, 78602, on october 4, 2022. unit 2 (jordan) informed she was walking eastbound in the parking lot from chilis grill and bar, located at 734 west sh 71, bastrop, texas, 78602 to her vehicle at discount tire, located at 716 west sh 71, bastrop, texas, 78602. jordan stated she was walking with her son, when a silver older model mercedes benz hatchback began to reverse out of the stall. jordan stated that she was behind the vehicle as it was backing out and the vehicle was not stopping. jordan stated she began to yell at unit one (1) to stop but it did not. jordan proceeded to kick the back bumper/hatchback of unit one (1). jordan confirmed her foot made contact with the rear of the vehicle; her son was not injured. jordan did not fall to the ground nor was she injured. jordan did not contact law enforcement or request ems at the time of the incident. the driver of unit one (1) made contact with her and asked if she was okay. jordan was unable to get a license plate or identifier on the driver. on october 5, 2022, jordan went to the doctor for pain to her leg and once at the doctors office she was informed to contact law enforcement for a report. a follow up investigation was generated at panda express and confirmed there were no cameras depicting the incident or facing the parking lot adjacent to sh 71 [roadway].

to d1 who was by his vehicle (u1). i asked d1 what happened. d1 stated he was [roadway] of the [roadway] of travel to get onto the main lanes. d1 stated he was speaking to his front right passenger occupant (p1) when he struck u2 (pedestrian) with his vehicle. d1 stated he did not know what or who he hit and immediately pulled over and called 911. i then spoke to p1 to ask what she had witnessed while in the front right passenger seat of u1. p1 stated she was sitting in the front right seat of u1, and was speaking to d1. p1 heard something hit u1. p1 did not know what d1 struck, but saw blood on the drivers side windshield. p1 told d1 to pull over, advising him he may have hit an animal or a person. both d1 and p1 provided me with their information. d1 also provide me with his insurance to u1. d1 had valid drivers license, and updated liability insurance policy. additionally, there were no signs of intoxication while speaking to d1. at this time, i observed u1 to have left front quarter damage to the headlight, front windshield, and driver side mirror. in the front windshield i also observed there to be blood and human flesh. i then walked down the [roadway] 410 to where ems was working on getting u2 (pedestrian) [medical facility]. i was able to get u2's information from her texas id. u2 was in critical condition and was unconscious at the time of the accident. safd medic #[medical facility] with life-threatening injuries. i contacted tid and north supervisor who were both en route to the accident scene. traffic investigator, det. j. coronado #2580 arrived and interviewed both d1 and p1. tid took over the investigation. csi, r. reuter #9413 processed the scene. sgt. hensley #3208 also made scene and was briefed of details. while on scene of the accident, ofc. j. ramos #[medical facility] where u2 was transported. ofc. j. ramos stated medical staff reported u2 to have several broken bones in both arms, and left ankle. u2 had also suffered significant blood loss causing her to be in critical condition. i collected and provided det. j. coronado with u2's dod identification. ofc. ratajczyk #1667 took custody of u2's personal items that were found at the accident scene, [medical facility]. after tid and csi were both finished processing the scene, d1 was given the [case id] and the contact information to the traffic investigation detail. per tid, u1 was operable and therefore, [roadway] off in u1 after investigation was completed. tid was also continuously notified of u2's medical status during the investigation. additionally, around the time of the accident several calls about a pedestrian yelling and walking in the roadway came out (sapd-2022-1345471). det. j. coronado was notified and would follow up with callers for that cfs. at this time, there is no criminal investigation. nothing further to report. bwc/coban available.
